analysis:
Examined scripts/resolve-provider-release.sh (head 11-117) and both test files.

Resolver changes:
- Master pushes now resolve staging only (head 20-25).
- refs/heads/dev pushes resolve dev only and set dev_push (26-31); other branches fail (32).
- A non-validation dev release requires dev_push (55-58), so master can produce dev only as an unpublished validation build.
- Dev pushes stamp -dev.branch.N (86-88). check-release-version.sh reportedly accepts the optional branch. segment (test-provider-identity.py head 128); that script is not supplied.

Unchanged: prod still requires a tag (67-70), and validation_only still requires a workflow_dispatch with env=dev (49-54). The RELEASE_RESUME_RUN_ID exec bypass (line 5) is pre-existing.

The pipeline tests (test-provider-release-pipeline.py) assert:
- the caller dev lane runs only for a dispatched validation build;
- release-dev-branch.yml calls the shared signing job with the Developer ID;
- all environments meet the self-updater designated requirement;
- verify-source receives RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT and runs master's scripts.

Not supplied: the workflow YAML (release-provider.yml, release-dev-branch.yml, caller), provider-release-resume.py verify-source, check-release-version.sh, and dev branch protection settings.

Integration should verify:
1. Whether verify-source constrains dev-branch provider code or only workflow source.
2. Whether dev-branch artifacts can be qualified (A-017) or accepted by production self-update or keychain groups.
3. That dev-lane secrets are environment-scoped (DEV_*) and never PROD_*.

findings.detail:
Head lines 26-28 add refs/heads/dev as a second branch whose pushes publish signed dev releases (dev_push=true; previously base lines 17-19 rejected every non-master branch). The pipeline tests state that the dev-branch lane signs with the real Developer ID and that every environment's final app meets the self-updater designated requirement (identifier io.darkbloom.provider, team SLDQ2GJ6TL). The base already applied that identity to master dev builds. The new risk is that code merged only to dev now receives it too.

Trigger: anyone who can push or merge to dev, possibly under weaker protection than master, gets a published artifact with production-equivalent Apple code identity. That code can match any check keyed only on team/identifier, such as the self-updater requirement or keychain access groups like SLDQ2GJ6TL.io.darkbloom.provider. It can also be a candidate for build qualification.

The master-run verify-source gate checks workflow source, not dev-branch provider code. Impact relates to binary integrity and code identity (T-013/T-054, A-011/A-017).

Fix:
- Require dev-branch protection equivalent to master, or a distinct signing identity or bundle identifier for dev-branch builds.
- Ensure the self-updater and qualification gates reject -dev.branch.N artifacts outside DevNet.
- Update the threat model to record this new signing source.
findings.title: Dev-branch pushes now reach Developer ID signing and publication with a production-matching code identity
